title: Teaching herself piano; her mother's rule
summary: No musicians in her family; she taught herself from a found book of waltzes, took brief lessons and one year of college music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No. Nobody, I never heard of anybody in my family ever singing a note or playing a note or anything. But, when we moved to Greenville, Mississippi, we moved into a furnished house that had a piano in the living room. And sitting on that piano was a sheet, a book of like, Mama's Waltz, Papa's Waltz, Grandma's Waltz. I don't know who it belonged to at all. And I knew from going to school in Louisville, they taught little children to read the treble clef and to sing the parts. And so, we had already started the school. I took a piece of paper over, I didn't know the bass, you understand. I didn't know what the bass notes were at all. So, I took this piece of music over to the school and I asked the music teacher if she would show me on the piano. I mean, I should have said I made five lines on it and I made a note on the bottom line. And I asked if she'd show me where that note was on the piano. So, she did. And I took it back and I learned all those pieces in that book without, I have no ear actually. I shouldn't say I have no ear, but I don't have much of an ear for music. I can't play, remember pieces, I mean to hear pieces and then play. I can't do that. But I did learn to play all those pieces in that book. And at that time then, some of the people, the music teachers in town began to ask my mother if I couldn't take lessons. So, I took lessons from a lady there for a few months. And I don't remember what happened to her, but then a little time passed and then another lady I started taking music lessons from. I don't even remember the names. And I took lessons from her about five months. In the meantime, well, a little before that, my mother had bought a piano from a company in, I can't think of the name of that company in Memphis now. And as I was coming down the street, I saw a piano being moved into the house where my father had bought and we were living. And so, I went there, went in and there, my mother shook her finger in my face and she said, if anybody ever asks you to play and you say no, out goes the piano.

So, you can imagine, well, that's the way it happened. And I didn't take any more lessons because of my mother's long illness and various, various things until I went away to college and I did study just one year there. So, that's all the training or the musical instructions I ever had. And the rest of it I just learned by doing, I guess. I don't know what else. I never, as I said, I never was a pianist to say that I was a skilled pianist. But I, I, um, when I started with the organ, that's another, that's where my husband came into the picture. Uh, let me see, how is this about there? Where was I working?
